title: Independence of the sheaf K-flat resolution after exact point sections
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with final object $U$, let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and suppose $\Gamma=\Gamma(U,-)$ is exact on abelian sheaves. Let $R$ be a commutative ring with a map $R\to\Gamma(\mathcal O)$, choose $t\in R$, put $A=R/(t)$, and suppose
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O\xrightarrow{t}\mathcal O\longrightarrow\mathcal O'\longrightarrow0$$
is exact, with $\mathcal O'=\mathcal O/t\mathcal O$. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived extension $T=-\otimes_{\mathcal O}^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O'$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Exact sections induce $G:D(\mathcal O)\to D(R)$ and $G':D(\mathcal O')\to D(A)$ by restriction along the displayed coefficient maps. Put $L=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A$ [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. For a K-flat complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], put $C=\Gamma(P)$. The quotient identification $P\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'=P/tP$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and exact sections give $\theta_P:C/tC\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(P/tP)$. Define
$$\alpha_P=\theta_P\circ c_C:LG(P)\longrightarrow G'T(P),$$
where $c_C:L(Q_R C)\to Q_A(C/tC)$ is the universal derived-tensor counit of [lem-pc-mixed-tensor-pointwise-left-derived], specialized to the second factor $A[0]$ and followed by $C\otimes_R A\cong C/tC$, with $Q_R,Q_A$ the localization functors, and using the canonical identification $T(P)=P/tP$. Then for every chain map $h:P\to P'$ between such complexes,
$$G'T(h)\circ\alpha_P=\alpha_{P'}\circ LG(h).$$
For every complex $M$ and two K-flat resolutions $p:P\to M$, $p':P'\to M$ with flat terms, the maps
$$G'T(p)\circ\alpha_P\circ LG(p)^{-1},\qquad G'T(p')\circ\alpha_{P'}\circ LG(p')^{-1}$$
from $LG(M)$ to $G'T(M)$ are equal in $D(A)$. This equality is with respect to the canonical derived-extension identifications specified by $p,p'$; it asserts coherence of the displayed comparisons, without asserting they are isomorphisms.

proof.text: Exactness of $\Gamma$ on abelian sheaves applies to the underlying abelian sheaves of module kernels, images and cokernels. Thus $H^j(\Gamma K)=\Gamma(H^jK)$, naturally in every complex $K$: write cohomology as the cokernel of the map from boundaries into cycles and use preservation of kernels and cokernels. Consequently sections carry quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. Restriction of the scalar action changes none of these abelian groups. The localization definition therefore gives the functors $G,G'$ in the statement, with their action on a chain map given by termwise sections.

proof.text: For a flat-term model $P$, tensor the assumed short exact coefficient sequence with $P^j$; this stays exact by the definition of flatness. The identification $P^j\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'=P^j/tP^j$ is given locally by $x\otimes\bar b\mapsto bx\bmod tP^j$, with inverse $\bar x\mapsto x\otimes1$. A different lift of $\bar b$ changes the product by a multiple of $t$, and the inverse kills $tx$ because $tx\otimes1=x\otimes t=0$. These balanced maps commute with restrictions and descend to sheafifications. Exact sections now give $\theta_P:C/tC\cong\Gamma(P/tP)$, sending the class of a global section $x$ to its quotient section. This is $A$-linear and commutes with differentials. For $h:P\to P'$, put $u=\Gamma(h)$ and denote quotient maps by bars. Both $\Gamma(\bar h)\theta_P(\bar x)$ and $\theta_{P'}\bar u(\bar x)$ are the quotient section of $h(x)$. Since every class has such a representative, $\Gamma(\bar h)\theta_P=\theta_{P'}\bar u$.

proof.text:
Specialize the mixed-tensor left-derived functor and its natural counit to $R\to A$ and $N=A[0]$. Identify it with $L=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A$ through its specified derived-functor identification. The ordinary tensor identification $C\otimes_R A\cong C/tC$ sends $x\otimes\bar a$ to $ax\bmod tC$, with inverse $\bar x\mapsto x\otimes1$; the same balancing calculation as in step 2 proves well-definedness. For any chain map $u:C\to C'$, these formulas commute with $u$. Naturality of the counit therefore gives, in $D(A)$,
$$Q_A(\bar u)\circ c_C=c_{C'}\circ L(Q_Ru).$$
This assertion applies to arbitrary $C$; it does not require $\Gamma(P)$ to be K-flat.

proof.text:
Write $e_P:T(Q_{\mathcal O}P)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathcal O'}(P/tP)$ for the canonical K-flat computation of derived change of rings. These are the model identifications stipulated in the statement. Since $T$ is the left derived functor of ordinary change of rings, $e_P$ is its counit at a K-flat complex; in particular its naturality says
$$e_{P'}\circ T(Q_{\mathcal O}h)=Q_{\mathcal O'}(\bar h)\circ e_P.$$
Under $G'(e_P)$, the displayed $\alpha_P$ is $Q_A(\theta_P)c_C$. Apply $G'$ to this naturality equation and substitute step 2 and then step 3:
$$Q_A(\Gamma(\bar h))Q_A(\theta_P)c_C
=Q_A(\theta_{P'})Q_A(\bar u)c_C
=Q_A(\theta_{P'})c_{C'}L(Q_Ru).$$
By step 1, $L(Q_Ru)=LG(h)$. Conjugating by $G'(e_P),G'(e_{P'})$ gives $G'T(h)\alpha_P=\alpha_{P'}LG(h)$, the first assertion, for every chain map $h$ between flat-term K-flat complexes.

proof.text:
For the supplied resolutions $p:P\to M$ and $p':P'\to M$, take the finite category with three objects $0,1,2$ and only nonidentity arrows $0\to2$, $1\to2$. Its diagram of complexes is $P\xrightarrow p M\xleftarrow{p'}P'$. Apply the strict diagram replacement theorem on the given small ringed site. It supplies flat-term K-flat complexes $S_0,S_1,S_2$, arrows $a:S_0\to S_2$, $b:S_1\to S_2$, and quasi-isomorphisms $r:S_0\to P$, $r':S_1\to P'$, $q:S_2\to M$, satisfying the actual chain equalities
$$qa=pr,\qquad qb=p'r'.$$
On every cohomology object, $H^j(q)H^j(a)=H^j(p)H^j(r)$; all three maps other than $H^j(a)$ are invertible, so $H^j(a)=H^j(q)^{-1}H^j(p)H^j(r)$ is invertible. Likewise $b$ is a quasi-isomorphism. All five sources $S_0,S_1,S_2,P,P'$ satisfy the model hypotheses of step 4.

proof.text:
For clarity set $F=LG$, $H=G'T$, and $\beta(p)=H(p)\alpha_PF(p)^{-1}$. Step 1 and the localization definition make $F$ and $H$ functors on $D(\mathcal O)$; therefore they carry each quasi-isomorphism of step 5 to an isomorphism. Apply step 4 to $r$ and to $a$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta(p)&=H(pr)\alpha_{S_0}F(pr)^{-1}\\
&=H(qa)\alpha_{S_0}F(qa)^{-1}\\
&=H(q)\alpha_{S_2}F(q)^{-1}=\beta(q).
\end{aligned}$$
Indeed the first equality inserts $H(r)\alpha_{S_0}=\alpha_PF(r)$ and cancels $F(r)$; the third inserts $H(a)\alpha_{S_0}=\alpha_{S_2}F(a)$ and cancels $F(a)$. The same two cancellations with $r',b$ give $\beta(p')=\beta(q)$. Thus $\beta(p)=\beta(p')$. Every operation took place in $D(A)$ after the natural model identifications of step 4, so this is precisely the specified resolution independence. No inverse of an $\alpha$ was taken.
